title: Tunable inter-bilayer magnetic correlations and candidate multipolar physics in the van der Waals oxyhalides DyOCl, DyOBr, and DyOI
authors: F. C. Brooks, X. Bai, J. Bacsa, V. O. Garlea, S. Calder, N. Butch, M. B. Stone, M. Mourigal
abstract: Rare-earth van der Waals magnets provide a route to combining strong spin-orbit coupling, large magnetic moments, and reduced dimensionality in bulk crystals. We report a comparative study of the dysprosium oxyhalides DyOX (X = Cl, Br, I), which realize square-bilayer networks of Dy3+ moments separated by a tunable van der Waals gap. Structural refinements show that increasing the halide ionic radius strongly expands the inter-bilayer spacing while leaving the local bilayer geometry nearly unchanged. Magnetization and heat-capacity measurements reveal two low-temperature anomalies in all three compounds: antiferromagnetic order at TN ~ 7-10 K and a broader anomaly near TQ ~ 27-30 K. Single-crystal magnetization on DyOCl and DyOBr establishes a strong hard-c-axis anisotropy, consistent with crystal-field analysis of DyOCl, which yields an XY-like ground-state g tensor. Neutron diffraction shows long-range antiferromagnetic order in DyOCl, whereas DyOBr and DyOI exhibit sharp magnetic scattering coexisting with Warren-like diffuse features, consistent with robust in-plane correlations and imperfect inter-bilayer registry. Inelastic neutron scattering on DyOCl identifies crystal-field excitations near 25-30 meV and an additional magnetic mode near 10 meV whose temperature dependence is tied to the high-temperature anomaly. Taken together, these results establish DyOX as a tunable family of quasi-two-dimensional rare-earth magnets and point to candidate multipolar physics associated with low-lying crystal-field states. Direct probes of quadrupolar order, such as resonant x-ray scattering or elastic-constant measurements, will be required to determine the order parameter at TQ.
summary: This work characterizes the $	ext{DyOX}$ oxyhalides as tunable, quasi-2D rare-earth magnets. By measuring magnetic and spectroscopic properties, the authors establish evidence for distinct magnetic ordering and candidate multipolar physics linked to low-lying crystal-field states. The combination of structural tuning and advanced spectroscopy makes this a key platform for studying complex magnetic interactions.
main_problem: The study investigates the tunable inter-bilayer magnetic correlations and candidate multipolar physics within the van der Waals oxyhalides DyOX.
main_result: The $	ext{DyOX}$ series is established as a tunable family of quasi-two-dimensional rare-earth magnets, exhibiting distinct magnetic ordering and crystal-field excitations that suggest underlying multipolar interactions.
method: The research combines structural characterization (X-ray/Neutron Diffraction) with magnetic measurements (Magnetization, Heat Capacity, INS) and theoretical modeling (Hamiltonian fitting).
model_or_system: The system is the $	ext{DyOX}$ family ($	ext{X} = 	ext{Cl}, 	ext{Br}, 	ext{I}$), which features $	ext{Dy}^{3+}$ moments arranged in square-bilayer networks separated by a tunable van der Waals gap.
key_observables: Antiferromagnetic ordering temperatures ($	ext{T}_{	ext{N}} \approx 7-10 	ext{ K}$), a high-temperature anomaly ($	ext{T}_{	ext{Q}} \approx 27-30 	ext{ K}$), crystal-field excitations (25-30 meV), and low-energy magnetic modes (10 meV).
important_parameters: Halide ionic radius (tuning the inter-bilayer spacing), magnetic field strength ($\mu_0H \approx 0.1 	ext{ T}$ to $14 	ext{ T}$), and energy scales (10 meV to 30 meV).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed low-energy excitations are related to multipolar physics, although direct confirmation requires probes beyond the current scope (e.g., resonant X-ray scattering).
figures_summary: Figures show crystal/magnetic structures, temperature-dependent neutron diffraction patterns revealing magnetic anomalies, and plots detailing crystal-field level splittings under various theoretical operators.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes structural changes with halide size, measures magnetic transitions ($	ext{T}_{	ext{N}}, 	ext{T}_{	ext{Q}}$), probes excitations via INS, and uses theoretical Hamiltonian fitting to constrain the nature of the magnetic interactions.
why_interesting: The study provides a model system where dimensionality and magnetic interactions can be tuned chemically, offering insights into how low-dimensional quantum magnetism and multipolar interactions manifest in real materials.

Figure 2. Temperature dependence of the lattice parameters of DyOCl extracted from powder x-ray diffraction data collected with λ = 1.54 Å. Values for a and c are found via Rietveld refinement in space group P4/nmm. The vertical line indicates the onset of thermomagnetic transitions in the heat capacity of DyOCl.

Figure 3. Powder neutron diffraction pattern (red points) for (a) Dy- OCl, (b) DyOBr, (c) DyOI measured with λ = 2.41 Å in the para- magnetic phase at T = 40 K or T = 80 K with corresponding best- fit structural Rietveld refinements (black lines) and residuals (blue lines). Nuclear peak positions are marked as black ticks. Aluminum peaks are marked as red ticks. The residual between the model and the data is marked at the bottom of each panel as a blue curve. We note that low-angle peaks suffer some asymmetry from instrument resolution effects and stacking faults that are not modeled at that stage.
